explanation: Add the entries using a 64-bit accumulator and subtract n(n+1)/2, also computed in 64-bit arithmetic. The guaranteed single extra occurrence is the remaining difference.
correctness: The array contains one copy of every integer from 1 through n and one additional copy of the repeated value. Its total is therefore n(n+1)/2 plus that repeated value. Subtraction isolates the answer, and the declared n bound keeps both totals within a signed 64-bit integer.
walkthrough: For [3,1,4,2,3], n is 4 and the array total is 13. The required range 1..4 sums to 4*5/2=10. The difference 13-10 is the extra value 3. Both totals are evaluated in 64-bit arithmetic.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1. The promise includes every value 1..n and exactly one extra occurrence; the more general pigeonhole problem has a different contract.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: process the n+1 input entries; the range sum is constant-time arithmetic, or an additional n XOR operations in the XOR variants.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: scalar accumulator and range/loop variables, with no input mutation.
